'''Vladimir Michaelovich Miklyukov''' ({{langx|ru|Миклюков, Владимир Михайлович}}, also spelled Miklioukov or Mikljukov) (8 January 1944 &ndash; October 2013) was a Russian educator in [[mathematics]], and head of the [[Superslow Process]] workgroup based at [[Volgograd State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uchimsya.info/announc.php |title=Announcements of the workgroup "Superslow Processes" |access-date=2010-01-26 |archive-date=2011-07-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722005622/http://www.uchimsya.info/announc.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><!--- I failed to find any official evidence that there is a "laboratory", only "seminar" -->

==Biography==
In 1970, as a student of [[:ru:Суворов, Георгий Дмитриевич|Georgy D. Suvorov]] at [[Donetsk National University]], he defended his [[Thesis or dissertation|Ph.D. thesis]] ''Theory of Quasiconformal Mappings in Space''.<ref name="gen" /> In 1981 Miklyukov and his family moved to [[Volgograd]]. He was transferred to the newly built [[Volgograd State University]] where he became chairman of the Department of [[Mathematical Analysis]] and [[Complex analysis|Theory of Functions]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mf.volsu.ru/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=12&Itemid=28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110821210706/http://mf.volsu.ru/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=12&Itemid=28|url-status=dead|archive-date=2011-08-21|title=Faculty of Mathematics (Past And Present)...|publisher=Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Volgograd State University|language=Russian}}</ref>

His scientific research focused on geometrical analysis. At the same time, he was studying zero [[mean curvature]] surfaces in [[Euclidean space|Euclidean]] and [[pseudo-Euclidean space]]s, nonlinear elliptic type [[partial differential equations]] and [[quasiregular map]]pings of [[Riemannian manifold]]s. The main results of that work were related to the following groups of questions:
*The external geometrical structure of zero mean curvature surfaces in Euclidean and pseudo-euclidean spaces; spacelike tubes and bands of zero mean curvature, their stability and instability with respect to small deformations, their life-time, branches, connections between branch points and [[Lorentz invariance|Lorentz invariant]] characteristics of surfaces;
*Phragmén-Lindelöf type theorems for differential forms; [[Lars Ahlfors|Ahlfors]] type theorems for differential forms with finite or infinite number of different asymptotic tracts; generalizations of Wiman theorem of forms, applications to quasiregular mappings on manifolds; applications of isoperimetric methods to the [[Phragmén–Lindelöf principle]] for quasiregular mappings on manifolds.

From 1998-2000 Miklyukov was a visiting professor at [[Brigham Young University]].<ref>{{cite journal | journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=127|issue=9|date=September 1999|pages=2745–2754|title=Hardy's Inequality for W0 1,p-Functions on Riemannian Manifolds | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |first= Vladimir|last= Miklyukov|first2=Matti|last2=Vuorinen|jstor=119576|mr=1600117|doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-99-04849-2|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2009 Miklyukov was named a [[Honorary titles of the Russian Federation|Distinguished Scientist of Russian Federation]].<ref name="decr" />
